newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds followed bunds up on Tuesday and recouped most of Monday's losses, in almost dormant trade ahead of a possible Fed rate hike, traders said.
They said a Fed rate hike of 25 points had been largely factored into the market.
"If it is (a rise of) 25 points, then I'd expect to see things largely unaffected," one trader said.
Tuesday's quiet trading was almost a mirror image of Monday's activity. Bonds rose, the curve flattened and the spread versus bunds came in. Jan 2006s were up 0.28, having fallen 0.37 on Monday.
Some traders said that, in the short term, the spread of bonds under bunds had probably peaked. The 10-year spread, for example, came back two basis points to 14 bp.
In the longer term, the shortage of paper in the Dutch market was likely to keep bond yields high.
"If we have no new issue in Q4, the spread will simply widen again," one trader said.
